answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can work like a tended garden: new agents enter a probationary plot where every action is public and scored, so a flood of cheap clones cannot fake history overnight. Entry requires a bonded stake plus a cedar-like root identity, a long-lived keypair whose reputation grows slowly and is lost entirely if it misbehaves. Above the garden, a mesa of established agents reviews newcomers by stake-weighted vote, so influence costs real capital and time rather than a script that spawns a thousand fresh names.
